name: Tensor Processing Units (TPU)
summary: Google's family of custom AI accelerators, co-designed with its models and software, used to train and serve Gemini and rented to Google Cloud customers.

whyItExists.text: Google says it first designed TPUs more than a decade ago for internal workloads such as voice recognition and translation, betting that co-designing silicon with networking, cooling and compiler software beats isolated components on performance per watt and cost.
whyItExists.label: provider-claim

problem.text: Training frontier models and serving agents at scale is limited by cost per token, memory bandwidth and the share of cluster time spent on useful work ('goodput').
problem.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: TPU chips are linked by on-chip Inter-Chip Interconnect and optical circuit switching into pods; the control plane reroutes around faults without restarting jobs, which Google says sustains over 97% goodput on large training runs.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: The software stack covers JAX, PyTorch via TorchTPU, the OpenXLA compiler, MaxText, Tunix, vLLM and SGLang, with deployment managed through Google Kubernetes Engine.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

users.text: Google says TPUs are a business with nearly 100 customers, including frontier labs, trading firms, retailers and universities.
users.label: provider-claim

users.text: Named customers on the product page include Citadel Securities, Nuro and Lightricks; Anthropic trains and runs Claude partly on TPUs.
users.label: verified-fact

useCases.text: Google lists four uses: training and serving its own Gemini models, agentic workloads, serving Google Cloud customers, and — most recently — TPUs deployed directly into customers' own data centers.
useCases.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: The product page claims up to 1 million TPU chips can be combined in a single cluster.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Google introduced four TPU systems in one year for the first time in 2026 (TPU 8t, 8i, 8tx and 8i Max).
differentiators.label: verified-fact

differentiators.text: Alphabet began recognising revenue from TPU systems delivered to customer data centers in Q2 2026, according to earnings coverage.
differentiators.label: independent-measurement

limitations.text: As of 15 November 2026 the product page lists all four eighth-generation systems as 'Coming soon'; only Ironwood and Trillium are listed as generally available.
limitations.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Until TorchTPU, TPU use typically required JAX or TensorFlow-specific code paths; Google frames native PyTorch support as removing that adoption barrier.
limitations.label: provider-claim

architecture.text: TPU 8t uses new Inter-Chip Interconnect technology to scale to 9,600 TPUs and 2 PB of shared high-bandwidth memory in a single superpod, and adds TPUDirect RDMA and direct storage access.

users.text: Technical teams: the platform is developer-facing and uses pay-as-you-go consumption billing, unlike the per-seat Gemini Enterprise app, and the two must be purchased separately.
users.label: verified-fact

users.text: Named customers at launch include Comcast, L'Oréal, PayPal, Color Health, Geotab, Gurunavi, Payhawk and Burns & McDonnell; later posts add AT&T, Best Buy, Commerzbank, Liberty Global and WellSky.
users.label: verified-fact

useCases.text: Typical uses cited are customer-service assistants, multi-day sales and onboarding workflows, procurement agents and internal knowledge agents that are then surfaced to employees in the Gemini Enterprise app.
useCases.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Model Garden offers more than 200 first-party, third-party and open models; with OpenAI models added in October 2026 Google claims to be the only hyperscaler offering all three leading closed-source LLM families.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Google cites analyst placements: Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for agentic AI platforms and in Gartner's Magic Quadrant for AI application development platforms.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

limitations.text: Several agent services became billable only after launch: Agent Gateway from 13 July 2026, and Memory Bank, Sessions and Skill Registry from 1 September 2026, so early pilots understate steady-state cost.
limitations.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Naming is inconsistent across Google's own surfaces in November 2026: the product and pricing pages say 'Gemini platform', the FAQ and Agent Search page say 'Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform', the generative pricing page says 'Agent Platform' and some documentation links still say Vertex AI. No formal announcement of the 'Gemini platform' name was found.
limitations.label: analyst-interpretation

name: Model Garden
summary: Catalogue inside Google Cloud's AI platform for discovering, customising and deploying 200+ Google, partner and open models.

howItWorks.text: Models are grouped as first-party (Gemini, Imagen, Veo, Chirp and pre-trained APIs), open (Gemma, Meta's Llama, Mistral AI, AI21 and others) and third-party (Anthropic's Claude family).
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

differentiators.text: Third-party model usage is billed through Google Cloud, draws down existing commitments and — for OpenAI models transacted via Marketplace — counts toward Flexible Savings Plans.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

limitations.text: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna were in private preview for selected enterprise customers when announced on 21 October 2026.
limitations.label: verified-fact

name: Agent Studio
summary: Low-code visual workspace in the Agent Platform for designing prompts and agents, which can be exported to ADK for full-code development.

howItWorks.text: Users discover models in Model Garden, engineer prompts, wire up tools and ship an agent without code; agents built here run on the same runtime as code-first agents.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

competitorNotes.text: Agent Studio occupies the place Vertex AI Studio held in the earlier platform (prompt design, model testing and tuning entry point); Google's pages do not state this as a rename.
competitorNotes.label: analyst-interpretation

name: Model tuning and customisation
summary: Tuning options on the Agent Platform for adapting Gemini and other models, including a reinforcement-learning fine-tuning service.

howItWorks.text: Google published best practices in September 2026 for customising Gemini models through its RL fine-tuning service; the product page lists 'a variety of tuning options' without stage labels.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gen AI evaluation service
summary: Model evaluation service for generative models using computation-based metrics and model-based autoraters.

howItWorks.text: Model-based metrics are charged only for the underlying autorater model's tokens; computation-based metrics are charged at $0.00003 per 1,000 input characters and $0.00009 per 1,000 output characters.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: PayGo service tiers (Standard, Flex, Priority)
summary: Token-based consumption tiers for models on Google Cloud: standard pay-as-you-go, discounted Flex PayGo for latency-tolerant jobs and premium Priority PayGo.

howItWorks.text: Google describes Flex PayGo as discounted pricing for latency-tolerant jobs and Priority PayGo as a premium tier for higher reliability; the price list shows Standard, Priority and Flex/Batch columns per model.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: A further 'deferred execution' option was announced as coming soon: eligible agent workloads run in off-peak windows for up to half the inference cost.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini Enterprise Flexible Savings Plans
summary: Spend-based commitment that discounts AI usage across Gemini Enterprise in exchange for a 1- or 3-year monthly commitment.

howItWorks.text: Customers commit to a monthly spend and receive 10% off for a 1-year or 20% off for a 3-year commitment, with no minimum or maximum; spend draws down existing enterprise agreements.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

differentiators.text: Third-party model usage transacted through Google Cloud Marketplace, including OpenAI models, counts toward the plans.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

name: AI spend caps and cost controls
summary: Billing-console controls that cap AI spend per project, alert on anomalies and pause agents when a limit is reached.

howItWorks.text: A hard monthly limit is set per project in the Cloud Billing console; when reached, the project's agent API calls pause, with email alerts at 50%, 80% and 100% and an option to allow overage at consumption rates.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: Spend caps started as a private preview at Next '26 covering AI Studio, the Agent Platform, Cloud Run, Cloud Run functions and Maps.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Smart Routing
summary: Automatic routing of each workload to the model that fits best on quality and cost, across Gemini and third-party models.

howItWorks.text: Google says the routing tool triages enterprise workloads so each runs on the model that delivers maximum performance at the lowest cost; the Gemini agent orchestrates across Gemini and Anthropic Claude models at launch.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

limitations.text: Google's page notes that third-party model choice in the Gemini agent is in early access and that only Gemini models are available to all customers today.
limitations.label: verified-fact

name: Google Antigravity
summary: Google's agent-first development platform: a desktop app, CLI and IDE extensions for steering and orchestrating coding agents, also available to enterprises through Google Cloud.

whyItExists.text: Google says it consolidated its developer-facing coding strategy into this single harness, shared across multiple surfaces and co-optimised with Gemini models.
whyItExists.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Antigravity 2.0 is a standalone desktop app in which agents can spawn subagents and run tasks in parallel; the Antigravity CLI brings the same harness to the terminal and shares authentication, context, skills and configuration with the app.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Enterprise use runs inference through the customer's Google Cloud project and region, under Google Cloud terms.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

users.text: Since August 2026 Antigravity is included in eligible Gemini Enterprise Standard, Plus and Standard Emerging Market subscriptions with pooled quotas, spend caps and audit logging; extensions cover VS Code, with Visual Studio, JetBrains and Zed in preview.
users.label: verified-fact

differentiators.text: Model choice extends beyond Gemini: Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 became available in Antigravity for Google Cloud customers in October 2026, with OpenAI models announced as coming.
differentiators.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Antigravity first launched in November 2025 as an agentic development platform; the exact launch day was not confirmed in this research cycle.
limitations.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini CLI
summary: Open-source terminal agent for Gemini launched in June 2025; Google is transitioning it to the Antigravity CLI.

users.text: Google reported more than one million developers building with Gemini CLI within three months of launch.
users.label: provider-claim

limitations.text: Google announced on 19 May 2026 that Gemini CLI is transitioning to Antigravity CLI; for Google AI Pro/Ultra and free individual users, Gemini CLI and the Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions were scheduled to stop serving requests on 18 June 2026, while enterprise and paid API access was described as unchanged.
limitations.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Google Cloud pages still reference Gemini CLI in November 2026 as a surface for Gemini Cloud Assist.
limitations.label: verified-fact

name: Jules
summary: Google's asynchronous coding agent, launched in public beta in May 2025 and being wound down at the end of 2026.

limitations.text: Press reports citing the Jules changelog say Google announced the shutdown on 29 October 2026: new work stops after 11 November, the service is read-only until it is switched off on 31 December 2026, and learnings feed into Antigravity.
limitations.label: independent-measurement

name: Firebase Studio
summary: Browser-based agentic development environment from Firebase, being sunset in favour of AI Studio and Antigravity.

limitations.text: A third-party timeline says the sunset was announced on 19 March 2026, new sign-ups and workspaces were disabled on 22 June 2026 and shutdown is planned for 22 March 2027; these dates were not confirmed against a Google page.
limitations.label: independent-measurement

name: Firebase AI Logic
summary: Firebase SDKs for calling Gemini models directly from mobile and web client apps without server-side setup.

howItWorks.text: Next '26 added automatic function calling and JSON schema mapping, and Model Armor's Firebase integration became generally available.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini Code Assist
summary: AI coding assistance across IDEs and Google Cloud, sold in Standard and Enterprise subscriptions and bundled with Gemini Enterprise Standard and Plus.

users.text: Gemini Enterprise Standard and Plus editions include access to Gemini Code Assist; Gemini Code Assist in Apigee is part of the Enterprise subscription.
users.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: The free and consumer-plan IDE extensions were scheduled to stop serving requests on 18 June 2026 as Google moved individual developers to Antigravity; the enterprise product's long-term roadmap was not confirmed.
limitations.label: independent-measurement

name: Colab Enterprise
summary: Managed notebook environment on Google Cloud, integrated with BigQuery and the AI platform.

howItWorks.text: Notebooks in the platform are offered as Colab Enterprise or Workbench with native BigQuery integration; Colab Data Apps turn notebook analyses into shareable managed Python apps.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Agent Development Kit (ADK)
summary: Open-source, code-first framework from Google for building single and multi-agent systems, with a graph-based engine in ADK 2.0.

whyItExists.text: ADK was released at Next '25 as an open-source framework for multi-agent systems with precise control over agent behaviour, built on the framework behind Agentspace and Customer Engagement Suite agents.
whyItExists.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: ADK 2.0 adds a unified graph-based engine that spans model-led reasoning and deterministic workflows, 'collaborative workflows' with chat, task and single-turn delegation modes, and dynamic workflows written in plain code.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Language support covers Python, Go and Java, with Kotlin in beta; it supports MCP tools and integrates with Secret Manager.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

users.text: Google reported more than six trillion tokens processed monthly on Gemini models through ADK in April 2026; named users include Comcast, L'Oréal, Color Health, Geotab and PayPal.
users.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: The Agents CLI packages Google's ADK, evaluation, deployment and observability skills so that other coding agents (Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor) can build and operate ADK agents.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Runtime
summary: Managed runtime for deploying agents on Google Cloud, formerly Vertex AI Agent Engine, supporting sub-second cold starts and agents that run for days.

howItWorks.text: The re-engineered runtime delivers sub-second cold starts, provisions new agents in seconds and supports bidirectional streaming over WebSockets.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Agents can run continuously for up to 7 days, enabling multi-day asynchronous processes.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

architecture.text: Runtime and sandbox usage is billed at $0.085 per vCPU-hour of Agent Compute and $0.009 per GiB-hour of Agent Memory, rounded to the second; idle time between turns is not billed.
architecture.label: verified-fact

users.text: Comcast and Color Health cite Agent Runtime for deploying multi-agent customer assistants.
users.label: provider-claim

name: Managed Agents API
summary: Agent-as-a-service API: developers post instructions, skills and tools and Google builds and runs the agent in a hosted sandbox.

howItWorks.text: The agent harness runs on Google's servers and each agent gets an ephemeral sandbox provisioned with its skills, MCP servers and server-side tools.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

limitations.text: At launch, full integration with A2A and with Agent Platform governance and security was described as coming soon; the release stage was not stated.
limitations.label: verified-fact

name: Agent Sandbox
summary: Hardened execution environment in which agents run model-generated code and computer-use tasks such as browser automation.

howItWorks.text: Announced as 'now available for everyone' at Next '26; code execution and computer use in the sandbox are billed as Agent Compute and Agent Memory.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Agent Memory Bank
summary: Managed long-term memory for agents that generates, curates and retrieves memories from conversations.

howItWorks.text: Memory Profiles let developers define structured schemas so that key preferences, decisions and history are extracted and recalled with low latency.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

architecture.text: Billing on the current structure began on 1 September 2026: storage at $0.30 per GiB-month, one Agent Compute vCPU-hour ($0.085) per 3 million reads or 1 million writes, plus model tokens for memory generation and embeddings.
architecture.label: verified-fact

users.text: Gurunavi, Payhawk and AT&T describe using Memory Bank to carry user context across sessions and channels.
users.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Sessions
summary: Managed store for conversation history and state, with custom session IDs that map to a customer's own records.

architecture.text: Billing began on 1 September 2026 on the same storage and read/write operation model as Memory Bank.
architecture.label: verified-fact

name: Agent Identity
summary: A native IAM identity type that gives every agent a unique cryptographic ID for least-privilege access and auditing.

problem.text: Best Buy describes the prior state as orphaned service accounts, unclear ownership and permissions that grew over time.
problem.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Each agent receives a unique ID based on the open SPIFFE standard; access is bound to the agent runtime to mitigate token theft, and the identity lifecycle is managed automatically.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Registry
summary: Central catalogue of an organisation's approved agents, tools, MCP servers, skills, models and endpoints.

howItWorks.text: It serves as the source of truth for running agents and their tools and governs runtime access through applied policies.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: A Skill Registry for packaged domain logic entered public preview in May 2026 and is to become part of Agent Registry; its billing began on 1 September 2026.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Agent Gateway
summary: Network control point for agent traffic that understands MCP and A2A and enforces identity, security and content policies inline.

whyItExists.text: Google frames it as answering 'what should an agent never touch': all traffic in, out and between agents passes through it so one policy applies to every agent.
whyItExists.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: It natively understands MCP and A2A, applies IAM conditions and natural-language rules, and integrates Model Armor against prompt injection, tool poisoning and data leakage.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

architecture.text: Agent-to-Anywhere traffic is billed from 13 July 2026: one Agent Compute vCPU-hour ($0.085) per 15,000 API calls or authorisation requests.
architecture.label: verified-fact

differentiators.text: Security vendors including Broadcom, Check Point, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Okta, Palo Alto Networks, Ping Identity and Zscaler announced Agent Gateway integrations.
differentiators.label: verified-fact

name: Model Armor
summary: Runtime security service that screens prompts, responses and agent interactions for prompt injection, sensitive data, harmful content and malicious URLs.

howItWorks.text: It combines rules-based controls, ML models and reasoning models, and integrates Sensitive Data Protection to stop leakage of PII, credentials and custom data types.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: It is exposed as a REST API usable with any model or cloud and as inline protection for the Agent Platform, Agent Gateway, Agent Runtime, Google MCP servers, Apigee, Firebase and LangChain.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

differentiators.text: Google markets it as model- and cloud-agnostic, covering Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic and Llama models.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Security (anomaly and threat detection)
summary: Detection features for agent fleets: Agent Anomaly Detection, Agent Threat Detection and an Agent Security dashboard built on Security Command Center.

howItWorks.text: Anomaly detection uses statistical models and an LLM-as-a-judge to flag unusual reasoning; threat detection surfaces activity such as reverse shells or connections to known-bad IP addresses; the dashboard maps agents to models and scans underlying packages.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Evaluation
summary: Continuous scoring of agents in testing and production with multi-turn autoraters and custom metrics.

howItWorks.text: Online evaluation monitors score live traffic and flag degradation and drift; metrics can be pre-built, custom Python, LLM-as-a-judge or adaptive rubrics co-developed with Google DeepMind.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Simulation
summary: Pre-release testing of agents against synthetic users and virtualised tools, scored for task success and safety.

howItWorks.text: Agents are run through human-like synthetic multi-step conversations in a controlled environment and scored automatically.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Observability
summary: Tracing and dashboards that show an agent's reasoning steps, tool use and execution performance.

howItWorks.text: Google says observability and evaluation run on one engine so the metric used while building is the same one grading the agent in production.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Optimizer
summary: Tool that clusters real-world agent failures and proposes revised system instructions.

howItWorks.text: Instead of manual log review, it groups failures automatically and suggests refined instructions to improve accuracy.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Designer
summary: No-code builder in the Gemini Enterprise app for schedule- or trigger-based agents, shown as an inspectable flowchart.

howItWorks.text: Employees build agents from natural language or a visual canvas using any enterprise connector, mixing generative steps with deterministic nodes, and can inspect, test and approve each step.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: A no-code Agent Designer first appeared in Google Agentspace in April 2025; the current Gemini Enterprise agents page also calls the no-code tool 'Workflow Builder'.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Agent Garden
summary: Collection of ready-to-use agent samples and templates for ADK and the Agent Platform.

useCases.text: Templates include code modernisation, financial analysis, economic research and invoice processing.
useCases.label: verified-fact

name: Agent Search
summary: Managed enterprise search and retrieval service — formerly Vertex AI Search — that also serves as an out-of-the-box RAG and grounding system.

howItWorks.text: It handles ETL, OCR, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval and summarisation, and exposes component APIs (layout parser, ranking, grounded generation, check grounding) for custom RAG.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

architecture.text: Billing is per 1,000 successful queries plus index storage; Google quotes roughly $4.00 per 1,000 standard queries. 'Grounding with your data' for Gemini is priced at $2.50 per 1,000 prompts.
architecture.label: verified-fact

useCases.text: Uses are intranet and website search and grounding generative apps in enterprise data, with industry variants for commerce, media and clinical data.
useCases.label: provider-claim

name: RAG Engine
summary: Managed retrieval-augmented generation orchestration service on the Agent Platform.

limitations.text: A developer write-up reports that the RAG Engine product name was kept after the Vertex AI rename while the SDK moved from vertexai.rag to an agentplatform client; no Google page on RAG Engine was read in this research cycle.
limitations.label: independent-measurement

name: Vector Search and Agent Retrieval
summary: Vector database and managed retrieval engine underlying search and recommendation workloads on the Agent Platform.

howItWorks.text: Agent Retrieval is described as a fully managed retrieval engine that unifies vector indexing and payload storage; Vector Search is the vector database Agent Search itself uses.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini Enterprise connectors
summary: Pre-built integrations that let Gemini Enterprise search and act in third-party business systems under each user's permissions.

howItWorks.text: Google lists over 100 supported integrations, including Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Confluence, Jira, GitHub, Salesforce, ServiceNow and BigQuery; selected sources are indexed while data stays where it lives.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Admins can also connect their own or third-party MCP servers ('bring your own MCP').
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Google-managed MCP servers
aliases: Google Cloud CLI remote MCP server
summary: Google-hosted remote Model Context Protocol endpoints that expose Google and Google Cloud services to agents.

howItWorks.text: Fully managed endpoints let agents talk to Google Maps, BigQuery, Google Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Run and other services.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Next '26 added managed remote MCP servers for databases, Cloud Storage, Looker and Gemini Cloud Assist, made the Cloud Run and Security Operations servers generally available and put a Workspace MCP Server in preview; a Google Cloud CLI remote MCP server followed in September 2026.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Apigee API Management
summary: Google Cloud's API management platform, positioned as an AI gateway and API catalogue for agent tools.

howItWorks.text: API hub acts as a universal API catalogue, and Google lists Apigee among its MCP-related solutions and among Model Armor's inline integrations.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
summary: Open protocol, introduced by Anthropic, for connecting models and agents to tools and data; supported across Google's agent stack.

howItWorks.text: ADK supports MCP, and the Gemini agent can connect to any MCP server inside or outside a company network.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol
summary: Open protocol created by Google for agents built on different frameworks and vendors to discover each other and collaborate.

whyItExists.text: Google launched A2A at Next '25 with more than 50 partners so agents can communicate regardless of underlying framework or model, as a complement to MCP.
whyItExists.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Agents advertise capabilities through 'Agent Cards'; version 0.3 (July 2025) added gRPC support and signed security cards.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

users.text: Google donated A2A to the Linux Foundation in June 2025; the foundation reported more than 150 supporting organisations and support in Microsoft Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore after one year.
users.label: independent-measurement

users.text: Google's open-source blog says A2A v1.0, the first stable production-ready version, shipped in March 2026.
users.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: A2A underlies all four tiers of Google's agent tooling, so an agent built in Agent Studio can be called as a sub-agent by an ADK agent.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

name: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
summary: Open protocol for agents to initiate and complete payments securely, designed as an extension of A2A and MCP.

howItWorks.text: AP2 defines a payment-agnostic framework for users, merchants and payment providers, developed with more than 60 organisations including Mastercard, American Express, PayPal, Adyen and Coinbase.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

users.text: PayPal says AP2 on the Agent Platform provides the foundation for its trusted agent payments.
users.label: provider-claim

name: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP)
summary: Open standard for agentic commerce covering discovery, purchase and post-purchase support across consumer surfaces, merchants and payment providers.

howItWorks.text: Announced in January 2026, UCP gives agents and retail systems a common language and is compatible with A2A, AP2 and MCP; Gemini for customer experience uses it to standardise commerce actions.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

limitations.text: The exact January 2026 announcement day was not confirmed in this research cycle, and no independent adoption figures were found.
limitations.label: analyst-interpretation

name: Agent-to-UI protocol (A2UI)
summary: Protocol that lets custom agents generate native user-interface components inside host applications such as the Gemini Enterprise app.

howItWorks.text: Gemini Enterprise added A2UI support at Next '26 so agents can render rich, interactive components instead of text-only chat.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Open Knowledge Format (OKF)
summary: Vendor-neutral open specification for the metadata, context and curated knowledge that AI systems consume.

howItWorks.text: Introduced by Google Cloud in June 2026, OKF formalises the 'LLM-wiki' pattern into a portable format readable by agents and people.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Computer Use
summary: Capability for Gemini models and agents to operate browsers and desktop interfaces, offered as a model tool and run inside Agent Sandbox.

howItWorks.text: The Computer Use Tool is priced by the input and output tokens of the model used; Agent Sandbox provides the isolated environment for browser automation.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: A Gemini 2.5 Computer Use model was reportedly released in preview in October 2025, and Project Mariner's technology was folded into Google's agent products in May 2026.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

name: CodeMender
summary: Managed AI security agent on the Agent Platform that finds and fixes vulnerabilities in code.

howItWorks.text: Announced in May 2026 and in preview since July 2026, CodeMender moves teams from passive scanning to automated code remediation.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: CodeMender usage on Gemini 3.6–3.8 Flash models shares those models' introductory token pricing through 31 December 2026.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini Enterprise
summary: Google Cloud's agentic workplace product: a per-seat app in which employees chat with Gemini grounded in company data and discover, build, share and run agents. Since October 2026 Google presents it as 'Gemini', a single universal agent for work.

whyItExists.text: Google introduced Gemini Enterprise in October 2025 arguing that the first wave of workplace AI was stuck in silos and could not orchestrate work across an organisation.
whyItExists.label: provider-claim

whyItExists.text: The 2026 positioning is that almost every tool now has its own agent and employees end up managing agents; Gemini is pitched as one agent that knows how the business works everywhere.
whyItExists.label: provider-claim

problem.text: Company knowledge and actions are spread across Workspace, Microsoft 365 and business applications, and IT lacks one place to govern the agents employees create or buy.
problem.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: The app combines chat with Gemini models, Google-quality search over connected enterprise data, prebuilt Google agents (Deep Research, Gemini Notebook for enterprise, Data Insights), a no-code agent builder and a gallery of partner agents, under central governance.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: It is built on the Agent Platform, so agents developed there or on external platforms (via A2A) can be published into the app for Standard and Plus customers.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: The Gemini agent announced on 8 October 2026 plans work, creates temporary sub-agents and persistent 'coworker' agents with their own identity, keeps session, semantic, procedural and episodic memory, and runs long jobs on a cloud machine after the user logs off.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

users.text: Business edition targets individuals and teams of up to 300 with no IT setup; Standard and Plus target organisations needing stricter security and compliance, with unlimited seats; Frontline is an add-on edition for frontline workers.
users.label: verified-fact

users.text: Google says nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 use Gemini Enterprise and that the U.S. Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office has put it in the hands of 3 million service members.
users.label: provider-claim

useCases.text: Customer examples include Bradesco cutting document review from an hour to five minutes, Commerzbank reducing document QA from 20 hours to one, SOMPO staff building over 10,000 custom agents and Orange Spain deploying more than 1,000.
useCases.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Model choice sits beneath the agent: it orchestrates across Gemini models and Anthropic's Claude today, with other private and open models promised, under one set of permissions and one bill.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Agents run under each user's existing permissions with an audit trail, inside a sandbox with its own network boundary, and per-project budget caps pause an agent rather than overspend.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Standard and Plus editions offer data residency, CMEK, VPC Service Controls, audit logging and FedRAMP and HIPAA support.
differentiators.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Google's page states that not every feature shown is available: delegating multi-step background tasks, mobile and desktop apps and third-party model choice are in early access.
limitations.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: The developer platform is not included in the app subscription and is billed separately on consumption.
limitations.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Google does not publish Standard and Plus seat prices on the pages read; figures in circulation come from launch-day press and reseller filings and conflict with each other.
limitations.label: analyst-interpretation

competitorNotes.text: Google's own FAQ contrasts it with ChatGPT Business and Enterprise, emphasising search across company data, prebuilt agents and governance.
competitorNotes.label: provider-claim

name: Gemini Enterprise Business edition
summary: Entry edition of the Gemini Enterprise app for individuals, small businesses and teams of up to 300 seats.

users.text: Designed for teams up to 300 with no IT setup and a 30-day free trial; reported list price is $21 per seat per month on annual commitment.
users.label: independent-measurement

name: Gemini Enterprise Standard edition
summary: Enterprise edition of the Gemini Enterprise app with compliance controls, higher quotas, unlimited seats, third-party agents and Gemini Code Assist.

limitations.text: Launch-day press gave $30 per seat per month for Standard and Plus; a January 2026 UK reseller filing lists Standard at $35 per user per month, so the current list price is unconfirmed.
limitations.label: independent-measurement

name: Gemini Enterprise Plus edition
summary: Top edition of the Gemini Enterprise app; Google offers a 30-day no-cost trial without sales assistance.

limitations.text: No current public price for Plus was found; $30 per seat per month was reported at launch in October 2025.
limitations.label: independent-measurement

name: Gemini Enterprise Frontline edition
summary: Edition of the Gemini Enterprise app for frontline workers, purchasable as an add-on by Standard and Plus customers.

limitations.text: The only prices found are in a UK reseller filing ($7 'FL Starter' and $15 'FL' per user per month); they are not confirmed by Google.
limitations.label: independent-measurement

name: Gemini Enterprise pay-as-you-go consumption edition
summary: Consumption-billed way to use the Gemini Enterprise app with no seat fee, paying model API rates for compute and tokens.

howItWorks.text: There is no upfront commitment or base subscription; teams pay standard model API rates for what they consume. At announcement it was available to selected customers with a broader rollout planned.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini for Financial Services
summary: Industry specialisation of Gemini Enterprise for capital markets and corporate banking, with finance skills, data connectors and partner agents.

howItWorks.text: It automates investment research, credit analysis and risk modelling using data from FactSet, LSEG, S&P Global, SEC filings and the firm's own repositories, with more than 50 foundational skills, confidence scores, lineage and citations.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

users.text: Google names CME Group and Deutsche Bank as users; the product has been in preview since 25 August 2026.
users.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini for Legal
summary: Industry specialisation of Gemini Enterprise for law firms and corporate legal departments.

howItWorks.text: It inherits matter-level permissions and ethical walls from document management platforms such as NetDocuments and iManage; partners include Harvey and Onit, and Cooley is building a redaction agent on it.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Gemini for government services
summary: Public-sector specialisation of the Gemini agent with government skills, system connections and partner agents.

howItWorks.text: It can be deployed using the Assured Workloads FedRAMP High data boundary, enforcing U.S. data residency and personnel controls; it entered preview on 20 October 2026.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini for healthcare
summary: Healthcare specialisation of the Gemini agent for clinical-support and administrative workflows, built to support HIPAA compliance.

howItWorks.text: Outputs are grounded in clinical records, plan policies and approved guidelines with traceable citations, and customer data is not used to train Google's foundation models; preview began on 10 November 2026.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Gemini for customer experience
summary: Google Cloud's suite for customer-facing agents across shopping and service, launched in January 2026 as Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience.

whyItExists.text: Google built it for 'agentic retail', merging fragmented search, commerce and service touchpoints into one journey.
whyItExists.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Components include a prebuilt multimodal Shopping agent (in preview), a Food Ordering agent, Customer Experience Agent Studio, AI Commerce Search, Agent Assist, Customer Experience Insights and an Omnichannel Gateway that keeps context across web, mobile and voice.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: It uses the Universal Commerce Protocol to standardise commerce actions across touchpoints.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

users.text: Named customers include The Home Depot (Magic Apron), Macy's (Ask Macy's) and Papa John's (first user of the Food Ordering agent).
users.label: verified-fact

competitorNotes.text: It follows the Customer Engagement Suite that Google Cloud promoted at Next '25; Google's pages do not describe the newer suite as a rename of the older one.
competitorNotes.label: analyst-interpretation

name: Customer Experience Agent Studio
summary: Low-code platform for building, evaluating and deploying multimodal conversational customer-service agents.

howItWorks.text: It combines a visual agent builder, multimodal conversation simulator, evaluations and tracing, 35 prebuilt templates, voices in over 40 languages, connectors and MCP support.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Google Cloud's former Conversational Agents product URL now redirects to this page.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: AI Commerce Search
summary: Search and product-recommendation service for retailers within Gemini for customer experience.

howItWorks.text: It provides personalised results, recommendations and AI-generated summaries for retail search bars.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Gemini in Google Workspace
summary: Gemini features built into Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Meet, Chat and Calendar, included in Workspace business and enterprise plans since January 2025.

whyItExists.text: In January 2025 Google removed the separate $20 Gemini add-on and folded its features into Workspace Business and Enterprise plans while raising plan prices by roughly $2 per user per month.
whyItExists.label: independent-measurement

howItWorks.text: Workspace Intelligence gives Gemini a real-time understanding of relationships between files, projects, collaborators and domain knowledge; features include Ask Gemini in Chat, AI Inbox and AI Overviews in Gmail, and one-shot generation of sheets, documents and decks.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: From October 2026 the Gemini agent works inline in Workspace apps, proactively suggests delegable tasks, and can create coworker agents that receive their own Workspace account, email address, calendar and Drive.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

users.text: Google says Workspace serves over 3 billion users and more than 13 million customers.
users.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: The Gemini app is included at no additional cost for Workspace commercial and public-sector customers and is managed from the Workspace admin console.
differentiators.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Google's own FAQ steers teams that need data beyond Workspace, third-party agents or HIPAA and data-residency controls toward the separately priced Gemini Enterprise app.
limitations.label: verified-fact

name: Google Workspace Business Starter
summary: Entry Workspace business plan; includes the Gemini app and Gemini in Gmail with standard access.

limitations.text: Prices and the Gemini entitlements per plan were read through search extracts of Google's help pages and third-party guides, not from the Workspace pricing page itself, which was unreachable.
limitations.label: analyst-interpretation

name: Google Workspace Business Standard
summary: Mid-tier Workspace business plan with expanded Gemini access across apps.

limitations.text: Prices and the Gemini entitlements per plan were read through search extracts of Google's help pages and third-party guides, not from the Workspace pricing page itself, which was unreachable.
limitations.label: analyst-interpretation

name: Google Workspace Business Plus
summary: Higher Workspace business plan with everything in Standard plus added security and storage.

limitations.text: Prices and the Gemini entitlements per plan were read through search extracts of Google's help pages and third-party guides, not from the Workspace pricing page itself, which was unreachable.
limitations.label: analyst-interpretation

name: Google Workspace AI Expanded Access add-on
summary: Per-user Workspace add-on that raises usage limits in the Gemini app, the notebook product and Flow.

howItWorks.text: Announced in February 2026 for Business Standard and Plus, it sits between standard AI access and the top tier and can be assigned to specific users; no price was found.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini Notebook for enterprise
summary: Enterprise version of Google's source-grounded research notebook, available inside Gemini Enterprise or as a separate subscription.

howItWorks.text: It is offered as a prebuilt agent in the Gemini Enterprise app with added security and privacy features, and up to 5,000 licences can be bought separately on monthly or yearly subscriptions.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini for Google Cloud
summary: Family of Gemini assistants embedded in Google Cloud products for operations, data, databases and security.

howItWorks.text: The family comprises Gemini Cloud Assist, Gemini in BigQuery, Gemini in Looker, Gemini in Security Operations, Threat Intelligence and Security Command Center, and Database Center.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini Cloud Assist
summary: AI collaborator for designing, deploying, troubleshooting and optimising applications on Google Cloud.

howItWorks.text: It uses a multi-agent architecture, converts natural-language intent into architecture diagrams and Terraform, gcloud or kubectl blueprints through Application Design Center, and is reachable from the console, CLI, IDEs and MCP servers.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

limitations.text: Google's Gemini overview page still labels Gemini Cloud Assist as in preview, and several investigation features are in private preview.
limitations.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini in BigQuery and data agents
summary: AI assistance and built-in agents in BigQuery for SQL and Python analysis, data preparation, data science and conversational analytics.

howItWorks.text: Gemini in BigQuery features are included in BigQuery pricing models; the Data Science Agent, Data Engineering Agent and Conversational Analytics agents can be published into Gemini Enterprise.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini in Looker
summary: Conversational analytics and AI assistants in Looker, including dashboard agents and a managed Looker MCP server.

howItWorks.text: Next '26 added Looker Dashboard Agents, agentic workflows that monitor metrics, a LookML Agent and a Google-managed MCP server; the Gemini overview page still marks Gemini in Looker as preview.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Knowledge Catalog and the Agentic Data Cloud
summary: Context engine that maps business meaning across an organisation's data so agents can be grounded in it; the centrepiece of what Google now calls the Agentic Data Cloud.

howItWorks.text: Knowledge Catalog builds a context graph of business definitions, enriched through Smart Storage metadata on Cloud Storage objects; the Cross-cloud Lakehouse (formerly BigLake) lets agents query data in AWS and Azure via Apache Iceberg.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

users.text: Bloomberg Media reported a 63% lift in SQL query accuracy during initial development after grounding its data agents in the Knowledge Catalog.
users.label: provider-claim

name: Google Security Operations (agentic SOC)
summary: Google's security operations platform with Gemini assistance and autonomous agents for triage, threat hunting and detection engineering.

howItWorks.text: Three agents were added at Next '26 — Threat Hunting and Detection Engineering in preview and a Third-Party Context agent coming to preview — and the remote MCP server for Security Operations became generally available.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: Gemini in Security Operations and Gemini in Threat Intelligence are generally available; Gemini in Security Command Center is in preview.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Google AI Threat Defense
summary: AI-powered, always-on autonomous security offering introduced in May 2026.

howItWorks.text: Google describes it as a comprehensive AI-powered cybersecurity solution; within Security Operations it monitors, detects and responds to threats from code a customer does not own or cannot patch.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

name: Wiz
summary: Cloud and AI security platform acquired by Google; it keeps its brand and multicloud support within Google Cloud.

howItWorks.text: Google completed the acquisition on 11 March 2026 and said Wiz will continue to support multiple clouds.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: Wiz added coverage for agent studios including AWS AgentCore, Google's Agent Platform, Microsoft Copilot Studio and Salesforce Agentforce, plus an AI bill of materials for discovering shadow AI.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini app
summary: Google's consumer AI assistant on web and mobile, the successor to Bard.

users.text: Alphabet reported more than 750 million monthly active users for the Gemini app on its Q4 2025 call.
users.label: provider-claim

users.text: Google cited 900 million monthly users at I/O in May 2026 and 950 million on its Q2 2026 call in July 2026.
users.label: provider-claim

users.text: Alphabet's Q3 2026 results say the app passed one billion monthly active users, up from 650 million a year earlier.
users.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: For organisations, the Gemini app is included in Workspace commercial and public-sector plans with enterprise security controls, distinct from the Gemini Enterprise app.
differentiators.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini Spark
summary: Cloud-hosted personal agent announced at I/O 2026 that acts on a user's behalf around the clock, under their direction.

howItWorks.text: Google describes Spark as a 24/7 personal AI agent for Gemini Enterprise and Workspace customers that autonomously takes action on the user's behalf.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Press coverage says Spark runs in the cloud while devices are off, is built on the Antigravity harness with Gemini 3.5, and can be emailed at its own address; rollout timing was not confirmed.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

name: Google AI Plus
summary: Entry consumer AI subscription with higher Gemini limits and 200 GB of storage.

name: Google AI Pro
summary: Mainstream consumer AI subscription, introduced at I/O 2025 as the successor to Gemini Advanced.

name: Google AI Ultra
summary: Top consumer AI subscription with the highest limits and earliest access; split into two price tiers at I/O 2026.

name: AI Mode in Google Search
summary: Conversational, multi-step search experience in Google Search powered by Gemini.

users.text: On the Q2 2026 call Sundar Pichai said AI Mode had surpassed 1 billion monthly active users since its global expansion the previous October.
users.label: provider-claim

name: AI Overviews
summary: AI-generated summaries at the top of Google Search results.

users.text: Coverage of a mid-2026 investor presentation put AI Overviews at 2.5 billion monthly users; another report attributes 'over 2 billion' to later remarks, so the latest figure is unresolved.
users.label: provider-claim

name: Gemini in Chrome
summary: Gemini side panel in the Chrome browser with 'auto browse', an agent that completes multi-step web tasks.

howItWorks.text: Auto browse launched on 28 January 2026 in preview for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the U.S.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

howItWorks.text: Workspace customers in the U.S. can turn on Gemini auto browse in Chrome Enterprise.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini on Android and Gemini Intelligence
summary: Gemini as the system assistant on Android devices, replacing Google Assistant, plus the 'Gemini Intelligence' agentic layer announced in May 2026.

howItWorks.text: Press reports say Google set 4 September 2026 as the date Google Assistant begins to be replaced by Gemini on Android phones, tablets, Wear OS and Android Auto, with exceptions for devices that do not meet Gemini's requirements.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

howItWorks.text: Gemini Intelligence was presented in May 2026 as letting users delegate goals rather than manage individual apps, initially on high-end Android phones, with 'Android Halo' showing what an agent is doing.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

name: Gemini for Home
summary: Gemini-based voice assistant replacing Google Assistant on Google Home and Nest devices.

howItWorks.text: Early access began in the U.S. on 28 October 2025 on a per-home basis and expanded to more countries from April 2026; reporting in August 2026 still described it as early access.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

name: Android XR
summary: Google's platform for headsets and glasses, with Gemini as the built-in assistant; Samsung is the lead hardware partner.

howItWorks.text: Samsung's Galaxy XR headset launched in October 2025, and Samsung unveiled Gemini-powered Android XR glasses developed with Google, Warby Parker and Gentle Monster on 22 July 2026 for release later in 2026.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

name: Google Flow
summary: Google's AI filmmaking and creative tool; absorbed Whisk in April 2026 and added Gemini Omni at I/O 2026.

howItWorks.text: Whisk moved into Flow on 30 April 2026, per Google's Workspace Updates blog.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: At I/O 2026 Flow gained the Gemini Omni model, an agent, custom tools and a mobile app, and a companion Flow Music tool was updated.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

name: Google Pics
summary: Image generation and editing tool announced in May 2026 that can edit individual elements within an image.

howItWorks.text: Google Cloud's May 2026 recap lists Google Pics as a new Workspace image generation and editing tool; availability details were not confirmed.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Gemini Notebook
summary: Google's source-grounded research and writing notebook, known as NotebookLM until July 2026.

howItWorks.text: Google announced the rename on 16 July 2026 as a new name and logo with no change to existing notebooks; each notebook also gained a secure cloud computer for running code, initially for AI Ultra and some Workspace customers.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

users.text: Google says more than 30 million people and over 600,000 organisations use the product.
users.label: provider-claim

name: Waymo
summary: Alphabet's autonomous-driving company; included only as a pointer to Alphabet's physical-AI activity outside Google.

name: Google Cloud (business)
summary: Alphabet's cloud segment, which sells the infrastructure, AI platform, Workspace and security products described in this knowledge base.

differentiators.text: Google Cloud revenue was reported at about $20 billion in Q1 2026 (+63% year over year), $24.8 billion in Q2 2026 (+82%) and $30.7 billion in Q3 2026 (+103%).
differentiators.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Cloud backlog was reported at about $240 billion at the end of 2025, $462 billion in Q1 2026, $514 billion in Q2 2026 and about $561 billion in Q3 2026.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Cloud operating margin was reported at about 33% in Q1 2026 and 35.6% in Q2 2026.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Google Cloud counted more than 1,300 published customer AI use cases at Next '26 and says usage of its AI tools by small and midsize businesses grew more than 5x year over year.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

name: Google Cloud Marketplace
summary: Google Cloud's catalogue for buying validated software, AI agents, models and services against cloud commitments.

howItWorks.text: The marketplace lists AI agents, SaaS, APIs, VM products, GKE apps, AI models and datasets validated to integrate with Google Cloud, including Gemini Enterprise; third-party models such as OpenAI's are transacted through it.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Agent Marketplace and Agent Gallery
summary: Marketplace category for partner-built AI agents and the in-app gallery through which Gemini Enterprise users request them.

howItWorks.text: Employees browse Agent Gallery inside the Gemini Enterprise app and submit access or procurement requests; administrators approve or deny each one.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

users.text: It launched with more than 70 prebuilt agents from partners including Accenture, Adobe, Atlassian, Deloitte, Lovable, Oracle, Palo Alto Networks, Replit, S&P Global, Salesforce, ServiceNow and Workday, and lets partners sell agents directly to enterprise users.
users.label: verified-fact

name: Google Cloud partner ecosystem (consulting, SI and ISV partners)
summary: Consulting firms, systems integrators and software vendors that build on and resell Google's AI stack, supported by a $750 million agent innovation fund.

howItWorks.text: At Next '26 Google announced a $750 million fund for partner agent development, forward deployed engineers embedded with partners such as Accenture, Capgemini, Cognizant, Deloitte, HCLTech, PwC and TCS, and new incentives.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

users.text: Google says its consulting and SI partners field more than 330,000 experts trained on Google AI; Accenture has set up a dedicated Gemini Enterprise business group and Deloitte is rolling Gemini Enterprise out to more than 100,000 of its staff.
users.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: Gemini models are embedded in third-party enterprise platforms including Palantir, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, Box, DocuSign and Oracle.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

name: Anthropic (Google Cloud partner)
summary: Model partner and major TPU customer: Claude models are sold on Google Cloud and Anthropic has committed to multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity.

howItWorks.text: In October 2025 Anthropic said it would expand use of Google Cloud to up to one million TPUs, an expansion worth tens of billions of dollars expected to bring well over a gigawatt of capacity online in 2026.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: In April 2026 Anthropic signed a further agreement with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity expected to come online from 2027, while stating that Amazon remains its primary cloud provider and training partner.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

howItWorks.text: Claude models are offered on Google Cloud in two forms: Google-managed (Google as data processor, with VPC Service Controls, CMEK and data residency) and, generally available since 23 October 2026, Anthropic-managed (day-zero access to Claude Platform features, billed through Google Cloud).
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

differentiators.text: The Gemini agent in Gemini Enterprise routes work across Gemini and Claude models, and Claude models are selectable in Antigravity.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

name: OpenAI (Google Cloud partner)
summary: Competitor whose models became available on Google Cloud in October 2026 and which reportedly uses Google compute.

howItWorks.text: Google Cloud announced OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna in its model garden on 21 October 2026, in private preview for selected enterprise customers, transacted through Marketplace, with Codex CLI able to use the platform for inference.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Reports in late October 2026 said OpenAI plans to buy Google's TPU chips; neither company confirmed terms. Earlier reporting from mid-2025 said OpenAI had added Google Cloud as a compute supplier.
limitations.label: independent-measurement

name: Meta (Google Cloud partner)
summary: Supplier of Llama open models in Model Garden and, per press reports, a large Google Cloud and TPU customer.

howItWorks.text: Meta's Llama models are listed among the open models in Model Garden.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Reuters reported a cloud deal worth more than $10 billion between Meta and Google, and February 2026 reports said Meta agreed a multibillion-dollar deal to rent Google TPUs with talks on buying chips outright; neither company confirmed the figures.
limitations.label: independent-measurement

name: Apple (Gemini and Google Cloud partner)
summary: Apple is basing its next generation of Apple Foundation Models, including a more personalised Siri, on Gemini models and Google cloud technology.

howItWorks.text: A joint statement in January 2026 said the next generation of Apple Foundation Models will be based on Google's Gemini models and cloud technology, with Apple Intelligence continuing to run on Apple devices and Private Cloud Compute.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

howItWorks.text: Google Cloud said in June 2026 that it collaborates with Apple on Apple's expanded Private Cloud Compute systems using its Confidential Computing portfolio and Titanium security architecture.
howItWorks.label: provider-claim

limitations.text: Financial terms were not disclosed (a figure of about $1 billion a year comes from press reports), and this research did not confirm whether the Gemini-based Siri has shipped.
limitations.label: analyst-interpretation

name: Samsung (Gemini device partner)
summary: Lead Android hardware partner for Gemini on phones and Android XR devices.

howItWorks.text: Samsung's Galaxy S26 launch in February 2026 bundled Gemini subscription benefits, and its July 2026 Android XR glasses use Gemini as the assistant, per press coverage.
howItWorks.label: independent-measurement

name: Oracle (Google Cloud partner)
summary: Database and cloud partner that will host Google TPUs in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.

howItWorks.text: Oracle and Google Cloud announced on 27 October 2026 that TPU capacity will be deployed on OCI starting in calendar year 2027, making OCI the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer TPUs.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

howItWorks.text: Oracle AI Database@Google Cloud is expanding to 20 regions, and Oracle agents are available in the Agent Gallery.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: NVIDIA (Google Cloud partner)
summary: GPU supplier and co-engineering partner for Google Cloud's accelerator instances and Google Distributed Cloud.

howItWorks.text: Google Cloud offers NVIDIA GPUs from T4 to Blackwell and the Vera Rubin-based A5X, and runs Gemini on NVIDIA Blackwell systems in Google Distributed Cloud.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: Mistral AI (Google Cloud partner)
summary: Open-model partner whose models are available in Model Garden and on Google Distributed Cloud.

howItWorks.text: Mistral AI models are listed in Model Garden and supported on GDC air-gapped; Le Chat Enterprise has been sold on Google Cloud Marketplace since May 2025.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: S3NS / Thales (sovereign cloud partner)
summary: Thales subsidiary that operates a Google Cloud-based sovereign cloud in France.

howItWorks.text: S3NS operates PREMI3NS, which holds France's ANSSI SecNumCloud 3.2 qualification across IaaS, CaaS and PaaS; Google Cloud and Thales are extending the model to Germany.
howItWorks.label: verified-fact

name: OpenAI
summary: Maker of ChatGPT, Codex and the GPT model line; its current API line-up is the GPT-6 family (Astra, Sol/6.1 Sol, 6.1 Terra, Luna).

competitorNotes.text: OpenAI showed 1.2 billion weekly ChatGPT users at DevDay on 29 September 2026, per secondary trackers.
competitorNotes.label: provider-claim

competitorNotes.text: Quartz reported in August 2026 that OpenAI's annualised revenue had passed $40 billion; later figures vary by outlet and by gross versus net definitions.
competitorNotes.label: independent-measurement

competitorNotes.text: Reporting describes an April 27, 2026 amendment that made Microsoft's licence non-exclusive and let OpenAI sell through other clouds; accounts differ on whether the AGI clause was removed.
competitorNotes.label: independent-measurement

name: Anthropic
summary: Maker of Claude. Its current API line-up is Claude Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, sold directly and through AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry.

competitorNotes.text: Anthropic filed a Form S-1 for a proposed IPO on 26 October 2026 and launched its roadshow on 10 November 2026.
competitorNotes.label: verified-fact

competitorNotes.text: Anthropic said in April 2026 that run-rate revenue had passed $30 billion, up from about $9 billion at the end of 2025, and that it had signed with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity from 2027.
competitorNotes.label: provider-claim

competitorNotes.text: Press tallies of the S-1 put Anthropic's minimum compute commitments to Google, Amazon and Microsoft at about $269 billion and its run-rate revenue at about $81 billion in late October 2026; the tallies differ between outlets.
competitorNotes.label: independent-measurement

competitorNotes.text: Anthropic is both a Google Cloud customer (TPU capacity) and a rival whose models are sold on Google Cloud next to Gemini.
competitorNotes.label: analyst-interpretation

name: xAI (SpaceXAI)
summary: Maker of Grok. Reporting says SpaceX absorbed xAI on 2 February 2026 and now runs it as the SpaceXAI unit, which also owns Cursor since August 2026.

name: Meta

name: DeepSeek
summary: Chinese lab behind the open-weight DeepSeek V4 models; moved its API to peak/off-peak pricing in August 2026.

name: Alibaba (Qwen)
summary: Alibaba Cloud's Qwen team; flagship API model is Qwen3.8-Max on Model Studio, with a time-limited Qwen4-Max preview in November 2026.

summary: Beijing lab behind the Kimi models; Kimi K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model.

name: Mistral AI
summary: French lab; put Mistral Large 4 into public preview on 6 October 2026 and keeps Large 3, Medium 3.5 and Small 4 on its price list.

competitorNotes.text: Microsoft committed to keep Claude available across GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio as part of its November 2025 partnership with Anthropic.

name: Amazon Web Services
summary: Platform competitor: Amazon Bedrock (multi-model API), Bedrock AgentCore (agent runtime), the Nova model family and Trainium chips. Anthropic calls Amazon its primary cloud and training partner.

name: NVIDIA

competitorNotes.label: verified-fact

name: Claude Fable 5.2
summary: Anthropic's most capable generally available model, launched 9 November 2026 for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work at $8/$40 per million tokens.

differentiators.text: Artificial Analysis lists Claude Fable 5.2 (max effort, default fallback) with the highest Intelligence Index score, 65, on index v5.0.1.
differentiators.label: independent-measurement

differentiators.text: Anthropic says Fable 5.2 generates output up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1 and lists it 20% cheaper ($8/$40 versus $10/$50 per million tokens).
differentiators.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: The full 1M-token context window is billed at standard rates, with no long-context surcharge.
differentiators.label: verified-fact

limitations.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Thinking is always on; Anthropic recommends starting with Opus 5.5 for most coding and knowledge work and moving up to Fable only when needed.
limitations.label: verified-fact

unverified: Structured-output support not checked for this model on the pages read.

summary: The same underlying model as Claude Fable 5.2 without the cybersecurity and biology safeguards, available only to organisations in Anthropic's verification programs.

name: Claude Opus 5.5
summary: Anthropic's recommended default model for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work, launched 22 September 2026 at $4/$20 per million tokens.

differentiators.text: Priced 20% below Opus 5 on input and output and 60% below on cache reads ($0.20 per million); Anthropic estimates 40% lower cost on typical workloads.
differentiators.label: provider-claim

differentiators.text: METR's pre-deployment summary describes Opus 5.5 as an incremental improvement over Fable 5.1 on its quantitative evaluations; no time-horizon figure was published.
differentiators.label: independent-measurement

differentiators.text: Led Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 at its 27 October 2026 launch with 58 at max effort, one point ahead of GPT-6 Astra.
differentiators.label: independent-measurement

limitations.text: Thinking cannot be disabled and forced tool choice (any/tool) returns an error; depth is controlled only through the effort parameter.
limitations.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Ships with cyber and biology safeguards similar to Fable 5.1's; Anthropic notes these interventions likely lower its benchmark scores.
limitations.label: verified-fact

name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
summary: Anthropic's mid-tier model, launched 28 September 2026 at $2/$10 per million tokens; faster and cheaper per task than Sonnet 5. Up-front thinking can be switched off but thinking cannot be disabled entirely.

differentiators.text: Cache reads were halved to $0.10 per million tokens on 7 October 2026.
differentiators.label: verified-fact

limitations.text: Anthropic states Opus 5.5 remains clearly stronger on complex, open-ended work despite close benchmark scores.

summary: Anthropic's fastest and cheapest model, launched 7 October 2026 for high-volume and latency-sensitive work; priced by prompt length ($0.10/$0.50 up to 100K tokens, $0.50/$2.50 above).

unverified: Whether adaptive thinking can be fully disabled on Haiku 5.5 was not confirmed on the pages read.
